On that committed capability: 5 mechanisms induced from 100 successful resource-A observations with evidence-derived confidence 0.956522 (Beta(2,1) posterior mean x leave-one-out consistency 1.0) and slots {collection, id, q, limit, auth_token}; 150/150 never-observed resource-B transfer tasks executed a bound mechanism with binding accuracy 1.0, kernel verification 1.0, 0 cold fallbacks and 1.0 HTTP request per task; abstention_precision 1.0 and false_accept_rate 0.0 on 60 negative probes; NC-SHUFFLED-INTENT transferred at 0.0 with abstention 1.0, so the transfer is carried by genuine intent structure; and all three preregistered baselines (B-COLD, B-LITERAL-REPLAY, B-RETRIEVAL-K5) recorded mechanism_success_rate 0.0. The incumbent reference curve matches the prereg expectation exactly (no distill_parameterized, distill confidence 0.5 < min_confidence 0.8, same-intent EXPLORE, paraphrased UNKNOWN, 0.0 EXECUTABLE with 0 HTTP requests). The claim is NOT advanced to VALIDATED because its own frozen gate failed. It is NOT marked REJECTED because audit.json validity_findings show both failing conditions have zero dynamic range on this substrate for ANY system, including a correct one (cold exploration already costs 1.0 HTTP request per read and per query because its first generic REST candidate matches the substrate API; the D6 cost criterion is likewise unreachable because B-COLD also costs 1.0 request per task on the positive-control task set). The prereg section 10 consequence 'parameterized inheritance is FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING ... the architecture must change to non-inheriting alternatives' is therefore not identified by this measurement and is not triggered: the economic half is UNMEASURED-RATHER-THAN-REFUTED, and the mechanistic half (D1, D2, D3, D4, D7) passed at the audited ceiling. EXPERIMENTAL, bounded, with the economics deferred to a discriminating substrate, is the only status that is simultaneously conservative and lossless.

Retention event, not an advance. C-PRODUCT-ECON is not a frozen claim_id of this packet (spec.json claim_ids = ['C-PARAM-INHERIT']), no Product-lane economics claim was adjudicated, and its ceiling is unchanged from EXP-PRODUCT-36129169543 (ACCEPT_INSTRUMENT_READINESS_ONLY, codex/claim_state.json latest_event_by_claim = HYPOTHESIS). The only new cost datum is substrate-bounded and must not be read as product economics: on this stdlib REST substrate B-COLD itself costs 1.0 HTTP request per read and query task and 1.64 per write task, treatment amortized cost is 1.016 (crud-write) and 1.667 (crud-read, query) times B-COLD, and measured break-even is 253.8 transfer tasks on crud-write and never reached on crud-read or query. No model tokens, no browser or network egress, no real-agent success, no latency amortization and no maintenance cost were measured, so the registered proposition 'SPIDER saves total cost per successful task after retrieval, verification and maintenance' remains untested and stays HYPOTHESIS.

Keep two recorded open product defects explicitly on the table rather than closing them silently: (1) the literal SpiderKernel.distill() path still hardcodes confidence=0.5 against min_confidence=0.8, so literal mechanisms still resolve to EXPLORE/UNKNOWN and only the parameterized path can execute; (2) literal mechanisms still persist the resource-A Authorization bearer token in a durable action_template (observed in artifacts/raw/literal_mechanisms.json) even though the parameterized path stores ${auth_token} and no live credential appears in any treatment artifact. The next product action is to obtain the discriminating economic measurement stated in next_question, after which promotion must be re-adjudicated rather than assumed from this packet's correctness results.
next_question: On a substrate that imposes genuine cold-discovery cost -- multi-step auth, pagination and schema discovery, such that the B-COLD no-memory baseline provably costs more than one request per task and the amortization comparison has dynamic range -- does the now-durable kernel distill_parameterized reach amortized_cost_ratio <= 0.85 against B-COLD, B-LITERAL-REPLAY and B-RETRIEVAL-K5 at matched end-to-end success and break even within a preregistered number of transfer tasks rather than the 253.8 measured here, while abstaining with false_accept_rate <= 0.10 when a slot is bound outside the observed support, under thresholds derived from that substrate's measured baseline cost and frozen before any arm runs?
reason: The measurement transaction was valid and is independently audited PASS. The producer applied the frozen seven-condition rule as written and reported FAIL (FALSIFIES) rather than reinterpreting it, and the auditor independently recomputed every condition and set a narrower claim ceiling than either the producer's outcome label or the prereg's consequence. D1 (success 1.0/1.0/1.0 vs >= 0.80), D2 (abstention precision 1.0 vs >= 0.85), D3 (false accept 0.0 vs <= 0.10), D4 (ECE 0.0435 vs <= 0.15) and D7 (null control: 0.0 success, 1.0 abstention, cost ratio 1.0) pass; D5 (1.02-1.67 vs <= 0.85) and the D6 cost half (2.0 vs <= 0.50) fail. Both failures share one cause recorded by the auditor: on this substrate the cold baseline is already at the per-task optimum (1.0 HTTP request for read and query), so there is no per-task saving to amortize a 100-request induction bill, and the positive control's cost criterion is unreachable for any system on the same task set. That is a measurement of the threshold's dynamic range, not a measurement of the mechanism. Three independent facts make the bounded reading safe rather than convenient: the substrate is a real reachable HTTP service with real ETag/304 and session-scoped auth, self-tested before any arm (not a synthetic or absent substrate); the incumbent reference curve was measured on the committed kernel and reproduced the prereg expectation exactly, which makes the delta attributable to the new kernel path; and the three preregistered baselines all scored mechanism_success_rate 0.0, so the treatment's 1.0 is not a permissive-matcher artifact -- confirmed independently by the passing null control. Two findings change the program's state beyond the claim verdict: the durable kernel capability now exists and is committed, closing the EXP-GRAPH-36118890504 defect that prior packets recorded, and three real product defects were found by running the experiment (string-only slot alignment silently drove the list-intent confidence to 0 and would have been published as a scientific failure; verbatim copy of a constant Authorization header into durable templates; volatile session metadata promoted to a hard precondition), each now covered by a unit test. The bounded negative on cost must not be inflated into the prereg's architecture-pivot consequence, and the bounded positive on mechanism must not be inflated into validation or product promotion: the claim stays EXPERIMENTAL, promote_to_product is false, and the falsified half is carried forward as an explicit open question rather than as a closed domain. Immediate chaining is false because the next measurement requires a new substrate with genuine discovery cost and pre-freeze threshold derivation, which is a NEW experiment needing a Global Research Director mandate, and because the external-baseline half of the economic comparison is owned by Intel and Frontier this cycle; this handoff carries the question for that decision instead of dispatching it.
